*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 None of the sampled passages in modern secondary literature directly examine Kv 18.2, as occurrences of the term in those sources refer either generically to the act of Dhamma preaching, to Vinaya training rules, or to homonymous modern works.

 Substantial shared segments also occur within the *Kathāvatthu* itself—most prominently with the *Dānakathā* (Kv 7.4), *Iddhibalakathā* (Kv 11.5), *Niyāmokkantikathā* (Kv 4.8), and *Vohārakathā* (Kv 2.10)—as well as the *Majjhimanikāye Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Mahāsakuludāyi Sutta* (MN 77), and the *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12) [DharmaNexus]. Additionally, DharmaNexus identifies machine-generated alignments with several Tibetan translation texts (D0160, D3996, and D0295) and the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (MĀ 43 in T 26) [DharmaNexus].
